column1: # What each door hands the DECLARATION for each of the eight forms.
# The registry row describes what a USER writes, and it is written per door.
# The declaration (`RuleOptionShape`, since the first cure package) judges a PHP
# value, after the door has had its way with it. Between the two stands a
# normalization that is different on every door, and a cross-check that ignored
# it would report a disagreement on every numeric key in the tree.
# The live example the round measured, and the one to check this table against:
# Both doors are right, and one declaration serves both — because a CLI door
# carries text and folds it back into a number before the declaration sees it.
#   The declaration, composed with its door's normalization below, must accept
#   exactly the `promised_forms` of THAT door's registry row.
#   yaml      the document, parsed. The rule config is not coerced per key:
#             WHOLE rule block written as a scalar, so the door is the identity
#             on the value of a key.
#             digits (with an optional sign) to int, any other numeric to
#             float, everything else left a string.
#             the numeric one split on a `.` or an `e` instead of on
# A CONSEQUENCE THAT IS NOT A DEFECT, AND IS NAMED SO NOBODY READS IT AS ONE
#   On both CLI doors `int` and `string-number` are THE SAME WRITE: a command
#   line carries text, and `7331` is the only way to type either. They are
#   therefore accepted or refused together there, always, and a cross-check
#   disagreement can never separate them. The registry says as much in its own
#   words — "CLI door carries scalar text only" — and both names appear in
#   `promised_forms` of every CLI row that admits a number.
#   It is not a measurement. The three normalizations were read out of the
#   product once and written here by hand, because a table derived by asking
#   the product would make the cross-check a measurement of the thing it is
#   checking. When one of them changes, this file is wrong until a person
#   changes it, and the cross-check will say so in the only way it can: a
#   disagreement on every row of that door at once.
#   door    yaml | rule-opt | cli-alias — the three doors of axis A
#   form    one of the eight forms of `forms.tsv`
#   seen    the value the declaration judges, written as a YAML scalar and
